Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: pricing + residency impact (post-demo)

Hi Lena — thanks again for the demo time earlier today. Quick recap and a handful of next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Nimble ask: EU data residency for PII-adjacent conversational traffic; target economics for initial pilot ~3–5M tokens/mo.
- Budget band you shared on the call: EUR 2.5k–4k/mo (you said you’d confirm if that’s per environment or total).
- Key Qs we promised to follow up on: 1) delta for EU-hosted vs US-hosted unit $/1M tokens; 2) committed vs on-demand unit economics for a 6–12 month pilot; 3) how reserved capacity and KV caching change unit price at 3–5M tokens.

Attachments I’ll send: a one-page regional delta summary and a workbook with a simple MAU/token forecast template (please populate the highlighted column).

Next steps (proposed):
1) We’ll send a preliminary pricing table (US hosted baseline + EU residency uplift + reserved capacity scenarios) by EOD tomorrow.
2) You share the MAU/token forecast sheet before our commercial sync (scheduled Thu).
3) Technical deep-dive with our infra lead (cc Ben) to validate networking & residency requirements — can we do that the week after next?

If any of that looks off, say so and I’ll adjust. —Mina

--

- The budget band I quoted (EUR 2.5k–4k/mo) is for the pilot environment only (we expect 3 environments eventually: staging, pilot, prod).
- For the pilot we’re most comfortable with a 6-month committed trial if the unit economics look reasonable.
- Procurement will need a committed vs on-demand comparison and an estimate of what EU residency will add to monthly cost (we’re sensitive to any +markup for regional hosting).

I’ll fill out the forecast sheet and share by tomorrow afternoon. For the tech deep-dive: Tue 3/21 or Wed 3/22 after 14:00 CET works for us.

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-12T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up: pricing + residency impact (post-demo) — preliminary math

Lena / Mina — looping Priyom for commercial ops validation. Below is an initial, illustrative unit-econ table (rounded) we can formalize in the attached PDF and workbook. Notes: baseline here is our hosted public API (US region); EU residency reflects additional infra and network egress controls (~+20% mid-point). Reserved capacity (6mo committed) shows typical discounting we can offer at pilot scale.

Scenario A — On-demand (US hosted): $950 per 1M tokens
Scenario B — On-demand (EU residency): $1,140 per 1M tokens (+20%)
Scenario C — 6mo reserved (US): $780 per 1M tokens (~18% discount)
Scenario D — 6mo reserved (EU residency): $920 per 1M tokens (reserved + residency uplift)

Illustrative monthly math (for 3M tokens/mo):
- A: 3 x $950 = $2,850/mo
- B: 3 x $1,140 = $3,420/mo
- C: 3 x $780 = $2,340/mo
- D: 3 x $920 = $2,760/mo

Operational notes:
- EU residency involves private subnet + KMS in-region and slightly higher provisioning (primarily infra + compliance + replication overhead).
- Prefix caching and request-level batching typically reduce billable tokens by ~8–12% on chat-heavy flows — we should model conservative and aggressive caching scenarios in the workbook.

Attaching the draft one-pager and the full pricing worksheet (redwood_eu-pricing-sheet.pdf). Priyom — if the math looks off let us know.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_eu-pricing-sheet.pdf (PDF)]

Forecast attached. Procurement has also asked: if we commit to 9M tokens over 6 months, do you have a mid-contract true-up or flat overage price? Also — can you confirm if quotations will be in EUR or USD? Our finance prefers EUR pricing for contract.

Timeline: procurement needs a commercial proposal next week to align with our internal budget review (target decision window 3/28–3/31).

I’m attaching our filled MAU/token sheet and suggested contract term (6 months, pilot).

—Lena
